page-title.purpose: Baloo 2 800, title case, gold fill with a 2px ink stroke and hard drop shadow, on a band-gradient pill plaque. One per route; stroked text is only page and section titles.

card-title.purpose: Baloo 2 800, uppercase, chalk on a band plate (or a meaning-colored plate). Every card header.

body.purpose: Nunito 400 to 600 for paragraphs and table cells, 65 to 75ch.

numeric.purpose: Tabular figures always. Jersey 10 pixel face only for scoreboard numbers (strength score, card number band, LED panel).

micro-label.purpose: Small caps voice for column heads and stat labels; never competes with the value.

shadows.name: shadow-1
shadows.purpose: Plate drop on every card, button and chip. Hard, zero blur.

shadows.name: shadow-2
shadows.purpose: Lifted plate: modals and the user's own team row.

shadows.name: bevel
shadows.purpose: Raised stamped-metal edge on every plate.

shadows.name: bevel-in
shadows.purpose: Recessed edge: inputs, pressed buttons, LED panel.

shadows.name: well
shadows.purpose: Recessed panel inside a raised plate.

shadows.name: shadow-glow
shadows.purpose: Focus: gold ring inside an ink ring, visible on turf, lavender and gold.

motion.name: interaction
motion.purpose: Hover, press and background swaps. Snap, not easing.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: The one interaction tic: a pressed plate travels down.

motion.name: bar-grow
motion.purpose: A data bar may grow once on load. No bounce, no overshoot.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: min-width: the trade calculator middle column turns sticky

breakpoints.name: strip
breakpoints.purpose: peer panels become a sideways scroll-snap strip with a jump bar

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: phone nav, filters toggle, vertical field

breakpoints.name: key-collapse
breakpoints.purpose: league key folds to one summary line

components.name: Input

narrative.overview:
A dynasty tier sheet rebuilt as a late-90s sports-game interface. Every surface is a physical plate stamped with a near-black outline, the ground is turf rather than a page, and selection is a gold fill you can see across a room. The reader is still an analyst mid-week, but the console he is sitting at is a Dreamcast, not a terminal.

The reference world is inventoried screen by screen in [BACKYARD-INVENTORY.md](BACKYARD-INVENTORY.md), including the IP boundary. Read that file before adding a component. This file is the standard; that file is the evidence behind it.

This replaced the previous "Tier Sheet, Live" standard on 2026-09-15, which called for graphite-on-obsidian surfaces, flat-by-default elevation, and no decorative gradients. Those three rules are now reversed on purpose. Anything in the repo still asserting them is stale.
keyCharacteristics: Light and loud. Turf ground, lavender plates, navy ink, gold selection.
Every surface is an outlined plate. A 2px near-black edge plus a hard bevel, on everything.
Nothing is flat. Every fill is a vertical gradient or a texture.
Selection is a gold fill swap with ink text, with two named exceptions (folder tabs and meaning-colored jump tabs, below). Never a tint, never a stripe, never an underline.
Ratings are discrete and countable. Five pips or a segmented meter, not a percentage.
Labels are quiet small caps, values are chunky. The label never competes with the number.
Chrome is physical. Folder tabs, stamped chips, an LED panel for the freshness readout.
Phone and desktop are both real. Cmd+K is canonical on a keyboard; thumb reach and swipe on a phone.

rules.name: The Gold-Selection Rule
rules.body: Gold plus ink text is the selected state for rows, nav, the Cmd+K result, the sorted column, primary and pressed buttons, and the user's own team. A 6% tint of an accent hue was the old answer and it was unreadable on a phone in daylight. Exactly two exceptions, and no others: - **Folder tabs select by lightening.** `.tab` and `.cchart-tab` go to a lighter lavender face with navy text, matching the reference's roster and PLAYERS tabs. The tab is part of the panel below it, so it takes the panel's face, not gold. (`CLAUDE.md` says the same; it agrees with this.) - **Jump tabs over a meaning-colored strip take that meaning's color.** On What to Look For, the phone jump bar's active tab fills with its panel's plate color (green, amber or red, below) and chalk text, so the tab and the plate it scrolls to read as one thing. The tab label always shows. A new selected state that is neither of these is gold.

rules.name: The Three-Pillar Rule
rules.body: still holds. Cornerstone Teal, Foundational Blue and Upside Green are the three category pillars. They appear as a triad or alone with role meaning. Never a fourth.

rules.name: The No-Decorative-Hue Rule
rules.body: still holds for the six semantic hues. Lavender, periwinkle, turf, gold, chalk and ink are chrome and may be used structurally. Teal, blue, green, amber, orange and red always mean something: a category, a tier, or, on panels that sort players by whether they help the user, for (green), mixed (amber) and against (red). League identity colors (`--lg`) are data labels that always sit beside the league name; they are not part of the palette.

rules.name: The Gradient Rule, inverted
rules.body: Every fill is a vertical gradient: panels, buttons, bands, gold, turf. They are defined once as `--grad-panel`, `--grad-btn`, `--grad-band`, `--grad-gold`, `--grad-metal` and `--grad-turf`, and a component uses one of those rather than writing its own. The one standing exception is the lightened folder-tab face, which is written in two places (`.tab.active`, `.cchart-tab.active`) and should become a token the next time either is touched. A bespoke gradient in a component is the thing to avoid now, not gradients themselves.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: is unchanged. Anything quantitative renders tabular.

rules.name: The Uppercase-as-Metadata Rule
rules.body: holds. Page titles are title case, like the reference's "Main Menu" and "Game Summary"; all caps there is reserved for team wordmarks. Player names, team names and body copy are never uppercase.

rules.name: The Stroke-Is-For-Titles Rule
rules.body: `-webkit-text-stroke` appears on `.page-title` and `.section-title` and nowhere else. Stroked body text is unreadable at small sizes and stroked labels turn a table into a poster.

rules.name: The One-Pixel-Face Rule
rules.body: Baloo 2, Nunito and Jersey 10 are the three families, which is the ceiling. A second pixel face, or pixel type on body copy, breaks it.

rules.name: The No-Blur Rule
rules.body: Shadow offsets are hard, with zero blur radius. A blurred shadow is the single tell that gives a retro plate away as a modern card. The only sanctioned blur is the modal scrim.

rules.name: The Press-Travels Rule
rules.body: A pressed button moves `translateY(2px)` and swaps to the inset bevel, so it looks physically depressed. This replaces the old 1px nudge and it is the only interaction feel tic in the system. No bounces, no scales, no color flashes.

dos: **Do** make tabular-nums the default for any column with numbers.
**Do** use gold plus ink text for every "this one is selected" and "this one is yours" cue. The user is the gold thread through the data.
**Do** put a 2px ink border and a bevel on any new surface. A borderless panel does not belong.
**Do** pair every tier color with the tier letter at full opacity.
**Do** use one of the six `--grad-*` tokens rather than writing a new gradient in a component.
**Do** reach for `.rating-track` or `.seg-meter` before printing a bare 0-to-100 score on a card.
**Do** keep shadow offsets hard and blur at zero.
**Do** prefer OKLCH for new colors; the hex frontmatter above is the approximation, and `css/styles.css` is the source of truth.
**Do** keep Cmd+K discoverable on every page.
donts: **Don't** use a blurred drop shadow on a plate. Hard offsets only.
**Don't** express selection as an alpha tint, a left stripe, or an underline. Gold fill or nothing.
**Don't** introduce a fourth pillar color, or a "warning teal" / "info teal."
**Don't** apply glassmorphism, backdrop-blur, or frosted panels. A plate is opaque.

**Don't** add bounce, elastic, spring, or scale-in animations. Interaction feedback (hover, press, background swaps) runs 80 to 120ms; a data bar may grow once on load at 240 to 360ms ease-out. The reference has snap.
**Don't** use em dashes anywhere. Use commas, colons, or periods.

**Don't** copy, trace, or approximate anything owned from the reference: the Backyard Football and BFU marks, the kid characters, the NFL shield, any team logo, or the italic "BACKYARD FOOTBALL" strip. The grammar is takeable, the assets are not. See [BACKYARD-INVENTORY.md](BACKYARD-INVENTORY.md).
**Don't** make this look like Sleeper. Retro game chrome is not mascot energy, and the line is that our ornament is hardware and stationery, never a cartoon character.
**Don't** make this look like ESPN or Yahoo. No ad-shaped containers, no tab-bar overload.
**Don't** make this look like a generic SaaS landing page.
**Don't** nest cards inside cards. A plate inside a plate is twice the outline and half the clarity; the outer one should be a layout region with no card chrome.
**Don't** let a restyle move layout. The features mapped in `.agents/feature-map.json` are the contract, and `verify-app.py` is how you find out.
